newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Jan 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Jan 3.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

At least 16 people were killed by floods on the west coast of the USA today, which have also forced thousands of people to evacuate their homes. The worst rain for 40 years flooded the city of Reno, Nevada, closing its casinos for the first time ever. Flooding has caused major roads to be closed in California, Idaho, Nevada, Oregon and Washington.
NORTH SEA SET FOR A BOOMING NEW YEAR

It is expected that the North Sea will undergo a boom this year, after a disappointing 1996. British, Danish and Norwegian oilfields should pump nearly 7 percent more crude oil this year, and oil prices should remain firm. Two weeks ago Gulf Canada, headed by James Bryan, launched a 432 million stg cash bid for Clyde Petroleum, the first major takeover attempt in the North Sea sector for four years.
EASTERN QUIET GIVES STERLING A BREATHER

Following a dramatic fall of almost two cents against the dollar in London trading yesterday, sterling held steady amid very little activity in the Asian markets, due to the closure of the Tokyo markets for the holidays.
